ratings_why.fun: Almost every card touches the shared clock, so the draft is full of puzzles, but the permanent board grows slowly and most of the payoff happens inside the fight.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because of a clock both sides' attacks advance and eggs planted inside enemy units. No tribe today makes the opponent's board the engine's fuel or its timer.

verdict_why: One real rules gap: Frau Wechselbalg and Mother Rohrsang both rewrite the same first friendly Chick, and the cards don't say which wins.

points.text: When the first Chick comes from a friendly host under Mother Rohrsang, say whether it is a plain copy, or a copy that also takes the host's keywords and a third of its stats. The Changeling build assumes the copy wins, but neither card says so.

Off-label gem worth naming in the builds: Frau Wechselbalg copying your Hawk-Barred Hen or Pipit-Moor Hen under Ottilie gives you a second Layer that re-fires at every Chime for the rest of the fight.

Mother Rohrsang laying into the Herald of Spring, with Frau Wechselbalg, makes a twin Herald whose first Chime buffs the board permanently again. A lovely hidden combo. Keep it, and give it a line in the risks.

A faster clock just wakes the Seven-Sleeper sooner for the same gains, so there's no tension. Giving it a payoff that rewards keeping it asleep, or lets it wake early, would turn its clock speed into a choice.

The best decision each turn is free slots against board units: Chicks need room, while the Bellows-Hall Tuner wants three Chime units beside it. Lean into that with one card that pays you for each empty slot.

standouts.why: Grand Horologe Ottilie Gugger joins the two halves of the tribe: every Start of Combat Layer, Hawk or Winder becomes a clock-driven engine.
The Bellows-Hall Tuner turns the board into an adjacency puzzle, with Little-Door, the Herald, the Hour-Bird and the Journeywoman all wanting the two seats beside it.
Frau Wechselbalg copies the host, so it works on both sides: against a tall enemy, or on your own best unit, including Start of Combat Hens under Ottilie.

weakest.why: The Pattern-Book Painter is a plain number-ticker with no interaction beyond feeding the Brood.
The Hour-Bird of the Tower is a generic Chime buff. Beside the Bellows it's fine, but it adds no new decision.
The Weight-Hanger has one job, dying in front, though its forced strike does pair with eggs nicely.

flags.note: Hawk-Barred Hen plus Ottilie keeps one enemy asleep all fight, while new eggs keep Heaving it. The only counterplay is killing the Hawk or the all-dozing wake.
The Herald of Spring between two Bellows, or twinned by Wechselbalg, gives every Clockwork a large permanent buff each fight. It's the tribe's main permanent runaway line.
Red-Mouth with Ottilie and several Hens floods Heaves each strike, as the design itself flags.
Which rule wins when Frau Wechselbalg's copy rule meets Mother Rohrsang's foster rule on the same first Chick.
